```
Run a command inside a workspace and stream its output.

The command runs over the same brokered connection as 'spin ssh', so it needs no direct
network access to the workspace. Its standard input, output and error are connected to
yours, and its exit status becomes this command's exit status.

A terminal is allocated when both ends are one - so an interactive program works and a
pipeline does not get control characters in its data. Force either with --tty/--no-tty.

Examples:
  spin exec my-workspace -- ls -la
  spin exec my-workspace -- npm run build
  spin exec my-workspace --tty -- bash
  spin exec my-workspace -w /srv/app -- git status
  spin exec my-workspace -- cat build.log > local.log

Usage:
  spin exec <workspace> -- <command> [args...] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help               help for exec
  -i, --identity string    Identity file (private key)
      --no-tty             Do not allocate a terminal
      --start              Start the workspace first if it is stopped
      --timeout duration   How long to wait for the workspace to be running (default 5m0s)
  -t, --tty                Allocate a terminal even if this one is not
  -u, --user string        User to run the command as (default "root")
  -w, --workdir string     Directory to run the command in

Global Flags:
      --config string    config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string    text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")
```
